exact_items: Reconciliation-readiness criteria must be specified: when is a project/run state ready for reconciliation after an account switch or degradation event?

Criteria list must be explicit and testable: all pending receipts committed, no open HITL requests tied to the old account context, permission snapshots revalidated under new account, active workers notified and acknowledged
This criteria list is the gate for resuming execution and must be normative in Contracts_V0.md and referenced by Multi-Account.md
notes: Reconciliation-readiness gate prevents silent execution continuation after account context invalidation — a behavioral safety requirement

exact_items: requested_account_id? alone is insufficient: must be paired with requested_account_binding (none | preferred | required)
none: no account preference; system uses default account
preferred: system tries requested account, falls back to default with degraded-mode flag if unavailable
required: system must use requested account; hard-blocks if unavailable, fires concern/blocked episode
This three-value binding model is cleaner than a bare optional field and must be the canonical model in Contracts_V0.md and Multi-Account.md
manual_preferred_account_id (set by user in settings) is distinct from requested_account_id (set per-run by the caller/dispatcher)
manual_preferred_account_id is a persistent user preference that provides a default requested account for runs that do not specify one
requested_account_id takes precedence over manual_preferred_account_id when both are present
This distinction must be clearly defined in Multi-Account.md and in the account-identity resolution chain
operational_identity block must be present in all runtime snapshots: run.started events, attempt records, receipt records, usage events, concern records, and attention items
The block must be a stable named inline object (not spread fields) so it can be referenced by name in storage and consumption contracts
Fields: effective_account_id, effective_runtime_id, effective_persona_key, execution_role, actor_kind, requested_account_binding, pressure_flags, degradation_flags
notes: Lowercase operational_identity (not OperationalIdentity) appears to be the canonical name in the ledger; both forms seen — must be normalized to one

exact_items: UsageRecord must include account_switch_reason? and switch_event_ref? fields
usage-feature.md wants UsageRecord to explain why account switched mid-run (for billing, audit, and anomaly detection)
but UsageRecord currently omits both fields even though account_switch_event family now carries the canonical switch explanation
Usage records for calls that occurred after a switch must carry the switch_event_ref linking to the account_switch_event record
Blocked/degraded reason fields in the effective-resolution record must be normative and explicit
blocked_reason_code is the canonical machine-readable reason; blocked_reason_detail is optional human-readable context
degraded_reason_code and degraded_reason_detail follow the same pattern
Both pairs must appear on the effective-resolution record, not scattered as ad-hoc strings in concern records, HITL events, or attention items
transport/upstream provider split in Models_System.md must be completed: add transport_host_id and upstream_provider_id as distinct identity fields in model configuration and in usage records
A model_routing_record must carry both fields so that locally proxied calls are attributed to the correct upstream commercial provider
Models_System.md account-health display for model-provider account degradation must reference upstream_provider_id, not transport host
Identity/Projection closure: all surfaces that display effective identity (Orchestrator, History, Ledger, Usage, Source Control, Widgets) must consistently show the operational_identity block
No surface may display implied identity (run-level default assumed) when the actual effective identity diverged from the default during the execution
This is the canonical readiness posture for multi-account correctness: every surface that could show stale or misleading identity must have an explicit trust-state / freshness contract
notes: This is the coherence closure for all identity work in wave-004: every surface must be provably correct or explicitly show freshness warning

exact_items: Projection closure for route payloads: every primary_route_payload on an attention item and every resume_url must be derivable from the canonical route payload schema
Any surface that accepts a route payload as input (deep-link, cmd.*.open_in_*, palette action, attention item navigation) must validate it against the canonical schema
Stale or malformed route payloads must surface a clear user-facing error, not silently navigate to the wrong surface
Projection closure for concern records: every concern must be queryable by source surface (Orchestrator, Run Graph, Usage, History), by owner, by severity, and by resolution status
The canonical concern record family must be present in storage-plan.md; currently entirely absent
concern_id must be stable and usable as a route payload object_id for deep-link targeting
notes: The canonical concern record family is confirmed absent from storage-plan.md — this is the most critical structural gap across all 10 shards
